summary: Running Springs sits at roughly 6,000 feet in the San Bernardino Mountains, which means summer highs averaging in the mid-60s while the valleys below bake past 100°F — a genuine temperature inversion that makes it one of Southern California's quiet altitude refuges. The San Bernardino National Forest wraps around the community on nearly every side, offering direct trail access into thousands of acres of pine and fir forest without driving anywhere, and the proximity to Lake Arrowhead and Big Bear creates a recreational corridor that few 4.2-square-mile towns can match. But this is unmistakably a bedroom community: there is no meaningful employment base on the mountain, so most working households face the winding descent down Highway 18 or Highway 330 to valley-floor jobs in San Bernardino or Redlands — a commute that can stretch dramatically during winter storms or holiday weekends. At a median home price of $373,300 against a median household income of $85,681, the price-to-income ratio lands around 4.4, which is moderate by Southern California standards but notable for a community with limited local commerce and a 14.1% poverty rate suggesting an uneven economic picture. The retail footprint is sparse — a handful of small eateries and provisions along Highway 18, the main commercial artery that doubles as the town's spine — and serious grocery runs typically mean a trip downhill. Running Springs delivers mountain living at a lower entry price than Lake Arrowhead, but the tradeoff is isolation that sharpens every time the road closes.
